title: Design exercise: SAA-4.3-S02
scenario: Tamarind Bay Bookkeeping is replacing its 15-year-old client-ledger system with a new build, and nothing from the old database will be migrated. Each ledger entry carries between 20 and 200 nested attributes that accountants filter on directly inside the stored document, month-end reports chain many joins and subqueries, and the firm's compliance vendor ships its fuzzy name-matching add-on, which must be loaded inside the database itself, only for one of the two popular open-source engines. The two developers have only ever run MySQL, and go-live is 6 months away. Finance wants a fixed-size managed instance with a predictable monthly cost.
constraints: Do not claim live AWS experience
The vendor's name-matching add-on must run inside the database, and the vendor supports it on one engine only
Finance wants a fixed-size managed instance rather than usage-metered capacity
Go-live is 6 months away and the team has no spare training budget beyond vendor documentation

rubric.label: The chosen engine supports the filtering on nested attributes and the join-heavy month-end reports, the record says how the vendor's in-database add-on would be loaded, and explains why the developers' MySQL familiarity does not override them
The record states the extra ramp-up risk from the team's MySQL-only experience and a mitigation that fits the 6-month go-live

constraint_reason: Mapped as design_exercise to complete skill coverage when no dedicated live lab step exists
